sections.h2: Who records a deed in Tuscarawas County, Ohio?
sections.html:
The Tuscarawas County Recorder keeps the land records for every parcel in the county, and its seat is New Philadelphia. The office's duties page says it makes a permanent record of each document that conveys or encumbers land, files it in archival form and keeps it open to the public. Fees collected go into the county general fund.

Indexing is the reason sellers should care. Each filing is indexed so a searcher can build a chain of title, which shows who owned the land and whether any debt or lien still sits on it. A buyer's title agent will run that search before closing, so a clean record speeds a sale.

The county also holds registered land, called Torrens land, and the recorder handles those certificates of title. Most house sales involve ordinary deeds, but a parcel with an older registered certificate needs extra attention from the title company.

sections.h2: What does the Tuscarawas County Recorder charge?
sections.html:
The recorder's page states the fee in one line: $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each additional page, with $4 for each marginal notation. The statute behind those numbers is Ohio Revised Code 317.32, which sets a base fee and a housing trust fund fee and lets a county add a document preservation surcharge of up to five dollars.

Tuscarawas County Recorder fees as listed on the county recorder page
ChargeAmount
First two pages of a document$39
Each additional page$8
Each marginal notation$4
Non-conforming document$20 extra

Source: Tuscarawas County Recorder.

For anything else, such as certified copies or plats, ask the office for the current amount, since the statute sets different rates for each service.

sections.h2: What kinds of documents does the Tuscarawas County Recorder file?
sections.html:
The recorder's page groups its filings by type. For someone selling a house, these categories matter most:

  • Deeds of every kind: warranty, survivorship, quit claim and sheriff's deeds.
  • Mortgages and the papers that change them, including releases, assignments, assumptions, subordinations and waivers of priority.
  • Land contracts, easements and leases, along with certificates of transfer and affidavits.
  • Plats and condominium drawings.
  • Liens such as mechanic's liens, notices of commencement, federal and personal tax liens and workers' compensation liens.
  • Military discharges, powers of attorney and trust records.

The page also carries a fair housing reminder: a deed clause that limits sale, rental or use of a home because of race, color, sex, religion, national origin, handicap or familial status is invalid under federal law and cannot be enforced.

sections.h2: How do you get a Tuscarawas County deed approved before recording?
sections.html:
A deed in this county is checked by the auditor's side of the courthouse before the recorder sees it. The auditor's office is in the Courthouse Annex at 125 E. High Avenue, New Philadelphia, and is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. The auditor's page has a Deed Conveyance and Transfers section with a step-by-step procedure, a conveyance requirements form and a separate procedure for mineral deeds.

  • The GIS and Map Office reviews the deed against the tax maps. It accepts deeds for pre-approval by email at the address on the auditor's GIS page, with the surface Conveyance Form, the Mineral Conveyance Form, or both.
  • The auditor's office completes the transfer and collects the conveyance and transfer fees.
  • The Recorder's fees are paid when the deed is filed.

Conveyance fees and the per-parcel transfer charge are set by the auditor, so ask the auditor's deed transfer staff for the current rates before you write the check. Ohio also lets a county levy an additional real property transfer tax under section 322.02, with a cap of thirty cents per hundred dollars of value. Under section 319.202, the buyer submits a statement of value, and the seller pays the conveyance fee.

sections.h2: Can you record electronically in Tuscarawas County?
sections.html:
Yes. Since January 20, 2026 the recorder has accepted all document types by eRecording. Conveyance documents have an extra step: the submitter uploads the pre-approval forms and supporting papers first, starting with the document type, and only then sends the conveyance itself.

The county lists five approved eRecording providers: CSC, Hopdox, Indecomm Global Services, ERecording Partners Network and Simplifile. A title company or closing attorney normally holds an account with one of them. An individual seller usually has the closing agent handle the filing.

Records can be searched through the county's cloud search, and the recorder posts instructions for registering an account and setting up a property alert. Ask the office how an alert works before relying on it to watch your parcel.

sections.h2: What are the county's size and history for a seller to know?
sections.html:
Tuscarawas County sits in northeastern Ohio with an area of about 571 square miles. According to Wikipedia, it was formed from Muskingum County in 1808, and New Philadelphia, founded the same year, is the seat and largest city. Dover and Uhrichsville are the other two cities. The Moravian mission of Schoenbrunn was founded near New Philadelphia in 1772, and the Ohio and Erie Canal came through in 1829 and 1830.

The county also has a visible Amish and Mennonite community, counted at 3,496 people or 3.7 percent of the 2020 population. For a rural parcel, ask the title company to check easements and any recorded survey.

sections.h2: What can a seller get from the Tuscarawas County GIS and Map Office?
sections.html:
The GIS and Map Office keeps the county tax parcel maps and sells printed copies. Its page lists a first county road map free and $1 for each additional one, a plat book of all 22 townships for $25, and tax maps priced by size:

  • 8.5 by 11 inches: $0.50 without a photo, $1 with one.
  • 11 by 17 inches: $1 without a photo, $2 with one.
  • 18 by 24 inches: $2 without a photo, $4 with one.
  • 24 by 36 inches: $4 without a photo, $6 with one.
  • 36 by 48 inches: $6 without a photo, $8 with one.

Surveys are stored by location and old tax map page. The office says surveys from 2014 on are online through the parcel viewer, and older ones still sit in drawers in the map office, with scanning going on as time allows. If a buyer asks for a survey of your lot, start there before paying for a new one.

The $20 non-conforming charge on the recorder's page refers to the state formatting standard in section 317.114, which sets type size, margins and ink color. Have the closing attorney confirm the deed meets it before filing.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show for Tuscarawas County homes?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau's QuickFacts page gives this picture for 2020 to 2024 unless noted.

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $185,400.
  • Owner-occupied housing rate: 68.9 percent, among 38,492 households.
  • Median gross rent: $908 a month.
  • Median household income: $65,044.
  • Residents age 65 or older: 22.2 percent.
  • Population estimate for July 1, 2025: 92,373, down 1.0 percent from the 2020 base.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 69.

Ask the auditor for the parcel's current value and the title company for the last recorded deed before you set an asking price.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Tuscarawas County?
faqs.a: The recorder charges $39 for the first two pages and $8 for each page after that. Each marginal notation is $4, and a non-conforming document carries a $20 fee. The auditor's conveyance fee is separate.

faqs.q: Do I need pre-approval before recording a Tuscarawas County deed?
faqs.a: Yes. Deeds are approved by the GIS and Map Office and the auditor before the recorder files them. The map office takes deeds by email for pre-approval, and mineral conveyances use their own form and procedure.

faqs.q: Can I record a deed electronically in Tuscarawas County?
faqs.a: Yes. The recorder accepts every document type through eRecording as of January 20, 2026. Conveyance documents must upload the pre-approval forms and supporting papers before the deed is submitted.

faqs.q: Where is the Tuscarawas County Auditor's deed desk?
faqs.a: The Auditor's office is in the Courthouse Annex at 125 E. High Avenue in New Philadelphia, open weekdays from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., and its website has a Deed Conveyance and Transfers page.

faqs.q: Does the Tuscarawas County Recorder handle registered land?
faqs.a: Yes. The office lists certificates of title to registered (Torrens) land among its filings. If a parcel carries one, tell your title company early so it can examine the registered record.
